title: 2026-10-31_Linux_P2P_Ransom_Botnet_Incident_Response_Scenario_29f
description: Investigate a Linux P2P Ransom botnet ransomware incident, identify indicators of compromise, and take appropriate containment measures.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The victim host in your network has been compromised by the Linux P2P Ransom botnet ransomware. This malware combines ransomware capabilities with botnet functionality, spreading through peer-to-peer networks and encrypting files on infected systems. The malware also has command-and-control (C2) capabilities, allowing it to receive instructions from remote servers and participate in botnet activities.

Your task is to investigate the incident, identify the indicators of compromise, and take appropriate containment measures.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

To proceed, ENTER the passkey 'start' and SUBMIT the credentials.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

To proceed, ENTER the passkey 'start' and SUBMIT the credentials.

levels.title: Identify the Command-and-Control Server IP Address
levels.content:
Identify the command-and-control server IP address communicating with the compromised system.

Hint: Check network connections and process activity logs to find suspicious outbound connections.
levels.solution:
To identify the command-and-control server IP address, you can use the following command:

```bash
ss -tulnp | grep -E 'ESTABLISHED|LISTEN'
```

The output should show a connection to the IP address 192.168.90.5 on port 4443.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check network connections and process activity logs to find suspicious outbound connections.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp | grep -E 'ESTABLISHED|LISTEN'` to identify the command-and-control server IP address.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for established connections to external IPs in the output of the command.

levels.title: Determine the Network Port Used for Suspicious Command-and-Control Communication
levels.content:
Determine which network port is used for suspicious command-and-control communication.

Hint: Investigate network traffic and process activity to identify the port used by the ransomware for C2 communication.
levels.solution:
To determine the network port used for suspicious command-and-control communication, you can use the following command:

```bash
ss -tulnp | grep -E 'ESTABLISHED|LISTEN'
```

The output should show a connection to the IP address 192.168.90.5 on port 4443.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate network traffic and process activity to identify the port used by the ransomware for C2 communication.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp | grep -E 'ESTABLISHED|LISTEN'` to determine the network port used for suspicious command-and-control communication.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check the port number associated with the established connection to the C2 server.

levels.title: Locate the Ransom Note
levels.content:
Locate the ransom note left on the compromised system.

Hint: Search the victim's home directory for files that indicate ransomware activity.
levels.solution:
To locate the ransom note, you can use the following command:

```bash
find /home/cyrano -name "RANSOM_NOTE.txt"
```

The output should show the file `/home/cyrano/RANSOM_NOTE.txt`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Search the victim's home directory for files that indicate ransomware activity.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `find /home/cyrano -name "RANSOM_NOTE.txt"` to locate the ransom note.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for a file named RANSOM_NOTE.txt in the home directory of the user cyrano.
